It is recommended that you keep notes about what you are investigating and what you find as this will make the process of creating your presentation and report easier. Please note that you _do not_ need to submit this file as part of your group project.



```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```


```{r load-lib, message = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
# Add any other libraries here
library(readr)
library(janitor)
library(ggplot2)
```


```{r load-data}
# load your data 
seoul_bikes_raw <- read_csv("data/SeoulBikeData.csv", locale=locale(encoding="latin1")) #extracting raw data, locale needed to be specified as error otherwise.
seoul_bikes <- seoul_bikes_raw |> clean_names() #cleaning names to snake_case, as column headings' words initially separated with space
seoul_bikes

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

seoul_bikes <- seoul_bikes %>%
  mutate(
    wind_group = cut(
      wind_speed_m_s,
      breaks = c(-Inf, 1, 2, 3, 4, Inf),
      labels = c("0-1", "1-2", "2-3", "3-4", "4+")
    )
  )

ggplot(seoul_bikes,
       aes(x = wind_group,
           y = rented_bike_count)) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "col",
    fill = "steelblue"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Bike Rentals at Different Wind Speeds",
    x = "Wind Speed (m/s)",
    y = "Average Number of Bikes Rented"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
